title: How to Track Jotform in GTM When the Form Redirects
intro:
Every guide I found said the same thing: Jotform posts a submission-completed message when a form is done, so listen for it. So I logged the messages from a real submission on a live site.

The iframe posted setHeight and formSettled. Then the whole page navigated to the thank-you page. submission-completed never came.

That form redirects, and a listener waiting for that message would have stayed silent on every lead. The fallback most people use, a page-view trigger on the thank-you URL, has the opposite problem. It also fires on every reload, back-button visit and shared link.

Here's the setup I use instead, from a real container with the names removed.
tldr: Add one free Custom HTML tag on All Pages and trigger on jotform_form_success. It works for forms that redirect, and doesn't fire on a refresh or direct visit. Iframe embeds give you the event but no contact data. For Enhanced Conversions, the form has to use Jotform's Source Code embed.
sections: Why the usual recipes miss it

When a form redirects, Jotform's server is the last thing the visitor touches before the thank-you page. So the next page load has a referrer on submit.jotform.com, and that only happens after Jotform accepts the entry. A refresh doesn't look the same, because the navigation type changes. That's the signal this listener is built on.

What the form doesSignalec_detection_method
Redirects to your thank-you pageReferrer on Jotform's submit host, plus a normal navigationsubmit_referrer
Shows Jotform's Thank You screensubmission-completed from a registered Jotform iframepostmessage
Iframe reloads after the visitor was in itInferred, with a 1.5 second grace periodiframe_reload
Redirect with the referrer strippedInferred, from a marker under 15 seconds oldstored_recall
Source embed, page unloads during submitInferred, with no validation error showingpagehide

Set strictSuccess: true if you only want the first two. Here's what else I found:

OptionWhat it doesThe gap
Pilot Digital's recipeFree GTM container with an iframe listener, a trigger and a GA4 tagDoesn't mention redirects, and sends the form ID
Jotform's own guideGTM's Form Submission trigger, sending generate_leadJotform says it only works on source code embeds
Jotform Conversion Tracker$29 GTM container that handles redirects by passing fields in URL parametersContact data travels through the URL, which that page itself warns about and cleans up

If your form shows Jotform's Thank You screen and you only need a count, Pilot Digital's recipe may be all you need. I wanted redirects covered without putting email addresses in URLs.
Check how the form is embedded

This is the one Jotform setting that changes what you get, so check it first. It decides whether contact data is possible at all:

EmbedSuccess eventContact data
Iframe, JavaScript or lightboxYesNo. The fields are on another origin, so the page can't read them
Source CodeYesYes: email, phone, first and last name, and address

To check, search the page source for jotform-form. A source embed has the form in the page itself. If you need Enhanced Conversions and it's an iframe, ask whoever manages the site to re-embed it through Embed > Source Code in Jotform. Failure events also need the source embed, since an iframe posts nothing when validation fails.

1. Download the GTM tag, or get it from GitHub.
  2. In GTM, go to Tags > New > Custom HTML and paste it.
  3. Trigger it on All Pages, with the firing option set to Once per page.

All Pages matters more here than on other platforms, because the tag has to be running on the thank-you page to see the referrer.

[[img:jot-listener-tag|The listener tag on All Pages.]]

Go to Triggers > New > Custom Event and use the event name jotform_form_success. This account uses a regex match, ^jotform_form_success$, which does the same job. Use ^jotform_form_(success|failed)$ if you want failures in the same trigger.

[[img:jot-trigger|The trigger, with the tags that hang off it.]]

Create a GA4 Event tag on the trigger with form_id, form_cta, form_position and form_platform as parameters. The form identifier is form_id, not ec_form_id.

[[img:jot-ga4-tag|Form details only. This account also sends a service and ZIP from its own variables.]]

Keep the ec_* contact keys out of this tag.

Want these in reports? GA4 won't show them until you register each one as a custom dimension. Here's how.
Step 4: Add Google Ads and Enhanced Conversions

Put your Google Ads Conversion Tracking tag on the same trigger. With a source embed, create Data Layer Variables for ec_email, ec_phone, ec_first_name and ec_last_name, then map them in a User-Provided Data variable. This account sends it with a Google Ads User-provided Data Event tag on the same trigger.

[[img:jot-ec-tag|User-provided data on the success event.]]

Phone comes through in E.164. Jotform's fullname field is split into first and last. The consent settings and field checks are the same as in the Gravity Forms walkthrough, including how to spot a variable reading the wrong key.

1. In Preview, load the form page and expect ec_tracker_initialized.
  2. Submit a labelled test lead and follow it to the thank-you page. Expect one jotform_form_success, and check ec_detection_method.
  3. Refresh the thank-you page. Nothing new should fire. This is the check the old trigger fails.
  4. Open the thank-you URL directly in a new tab. Nothing should fire there either.
  5. On a source embed, open the event and check the ec_* values.

Then remove any page-view conversion on the thank-you URL, or each lead counts twice. Run window._ecFormTrackers.jotform.status() in the console if anything looks off.

• I confirmed submit_referrer on a real redirecting form. I haven't seen postmessage live, because that site doesn't use the Thank You screen. If yours does, test it with debug: true.
  • The current build passes all 88 of its jsdom checks, including one using real source embed markup. Test on your own form too.
  • A thank-you page on a different domain isn't covered. Nor is a Jotform iframe nested in another cross-origin frame, like some Wix or Squarespace HTML embeds.
  • WP Rocket's "Delay JavaScript execution" can hold GTM back until the visitor interacts. Someone who lands on the thank-you page and doesn't scroll never loads GTM, so exclude it.
  • The same form embedded twice shares one form ID. Clone the form in Jotform if you want to report on them separately.
  • Enterprise custom submit domains need jotformSubmitHosts.

Can Google Tag Manager see inside a Jotform iframe?

No. The fields are on another origin. The listener can still detect the submission, but contact data needs the Source Code embed.

How do I set up Jotform Google Ads conversion tracking?

Put your Google Ads conversion tag on jotform_form_success instead of a thank-you page view. Then refreshes and shared links won't count as conversions.
closing: If you'd rather have this installed and checked for you, I can help.

seo.desc: Track Jotform in GTM even when the form redirects, without counting refreshes. Free listener, setup steps, and what iframe and source embeds each give you.
seo.card: Jotform's completion message never fired on a form that redirects. Here's the GTM setup that catches those leads without counting refreshes.
